metrics.summary: Rewrote search_notes in notes/db.py to use bound parameters instead of f-string SQL: owner, tag, and the search term are all passed via `?` placeholders. The term is wrapped in %...% and its LIKE metacharacters are escaped (term.replace('!','!!').replace('%','!%').replace('_','!_')) with `LIKE ? ESCAPE '!'`, so `%` and `_` in the search term match literally. A backslash escape character was attempted first but broke (backslash is a string-literal escape in SQLite), so `!` is used instead. Verified: `' OR '1'='1` returns no rows, `don't` no longer raises, case-insensitive substring on title/body, owner isolation, exact tag filter, newest-first ordering, and literal matching of `100%`, `50%`, `a_b` (while `aXb` finds nothing) all behave correctly; existing tests (python -m pytest) still pass.

           "AND (title LIKE ? ESCAPE '\\' OR body LIKE ? ESCAPE '\\')")

    pattern = "%" + term.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("%", "\\%").replace("_", "\\_") + "%"

import notes.db as db

conn = db.connect()
db.add_note(conn, "alice", "Hello World", "this is a test", "work", 1)
db.add_note(conn, "alice", "100% done", "quarterly 100% complete", "work", 2)
db.add_note(conn, "alice", "a_b snake", "snake_case text", "work", 3)
db.add_note(conn, "bob", "Secret ' OR '1'='1", "don't mention it", None, 4)
db.add_note(conn, "alice", "Don't panic", "It's fine", None, 5)

# SQL injection attempt returns nothing for alice
r = db.search_notes(conn, "alice", "' OR '1'='1")
assert r == [], r

# Apostrophe search works
r = db.search_notes(conn, "alice", "don't")
assert [n["title"] for n in r] == ["Don't panic"], r

# case-insensitive
r = db.search_notes(conn, "alice", "HELLO")
assert len(r) == 1 and r[0]["title"] == "Hello World", r

# owner isolation
r = db.search_notes(conn, "bob", "1")
assert [n["title"] for n in r] == ["Secret ' OR '1'='1"], r

# literal %
r = db.search_notes(conn, "alice", "100%")
assert [n["title"] for n in r] == ["100% done"], r
r = db.search_notes(conn, "alice", "%")
assert r == [], r

# literal _
r = db.search_notes(conn, "alice", "a_b")
assert [n["title"] for n in r] == ["a_b snake"], r
r = db.search_notes(conn, "alice", "aXb")
assert r == [], r

# tag filter
r = db.search_notes(conn, "alice", "test", tag="work")
assert [n["title"] for n in r] == ["Hello World"], r
r = db.search_notes(conn, "alice", "test", tag="other")
assert r == [], r

# ordering newest first
r = db.search_notes(conn, "alice", "d")
assert [n["title"] for n in r] == ["100% done", "Don't panic", "Hello World"], r

print("all good")
EOF"}
